STEP 1 - Scene: This is a snack of cut cantaloupe (orange-fleshed melon) cubes on a white square-ish plate, photographed from above at a near-top-down angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a white dinner-style plate, roughly 26 cm across. Its visible width is about the size of a standard dinner plate, so I use diameter 26 cm. Area = 3.14 x 13^2 ≈ 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Cantaloupe/melon cubes (about 9-10 pieces, roughly 2.5-3 cm chunks, some with rind edges visible). No sauce or oil is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The melon pieces cover roughly 30% of the plate, concentrated in the upper-left half. Cantaloupe: ~30% (about 160 cm^2).

STEP 5 - Volume: Pieces are piled about 2 cm high on average. Volume ≈ 160 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 320 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut fruit bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 320 ml x 0.6 ≈ 190 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cantaloupe ≈ 34 kcal per 100 g. 190 g x 0.34 ≈ 65 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Roughly 10 cubes of cantaloupe, about 190 g, is a plausible portion of a cup-sized fruit serving. Energy of about 65 kcal is consistent with melon, which is low in calories. Plausible.

Total: about 190 g, about 65 kcal.
